title: TorchGT: A Holistic System for Large-Scale Graph Transformer Training
problem: Existing graph transformers fail on large-scale graphs with millions of nodes due to heavy computation, limited scalability, and inferior model quality. Current systems cannot efficiently handle real-world large-scale graph datasets.
motivation: Graph Transformers surpass GNNs in graph learning but practical adoption on real-world large-scale graphs remains limited.
method: TorchGT optimizes training at three levels. At the algorithm level, Dual-interleaved Attention (a technique for processing graphs) exploits sparsity—most node pairs don't connect—while keeping the model accurate. At the runtime level, Cluster-aware Graph Parallelism splits work across multiple machines while minimizing data transfer between them. At the kernel level, Elastic Computation Reformation dynamically reorganizes computations to reduce memory access delays.
key_novelty: TorchGT combines three levels of optimization—algorithm-level sparse attention, runtime-level communication-efficient distributed parallelism, and kernel-level dynamic memory reformation—enabling large-scale graph transformer training.
contributions: Dual-interleaved Attention algorithm exploiting graph sparsity with preserved accuracy
Cluster-aware Graph Parallelism enabling communication-light distributed training
Elastic Computation Reformation for dynamic memory access optimization
62.7× speedup and support for graph sequences up to 1M nodes
limitations: Specific accuracy improvements and detailed comparisons with competing graph transformer systems not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: System-level optimization for large-scale graph transformers
